title: Interest Rate Risk Management
outcomes: Explain benchmark rates and the LIBOR transition.
Identify and measure types of interest rate risk.
Hedge with ALM and forward rate agreements.
Hedge with futures, caps, floors, collars, swaps and swaptions.

meta.exam_tip: In swap sums, compute the quality spread differential first, then design the flows.

concepts.title: Benchmark rates and the end of LIBOR
body: Benchmark (reference) rates are the base for pricing loans, bonds and derivatives; borrowers pay a spread in basis points over them.

LIBOR was discontinued after manipulation scandals; since 2022 markets use alternative reference rates based on actual overnight transactions and close to risk-free: SOFR (US, secured), SONIA (UK), €STR (euro area), TONA (Japan), SARON (Switzerland).
In India, benchmarks include MIBOR (FBIL overnight), T-bill rates, and the repo-linked external benchmark used by banks for loans.
concepts.analogy: Floating rates are benchmark plus spread — and the benchmarks have changed.
concepts.work: A US dollar loan now references SOFR, not LIBOR.

concepts.title: Types and measurement of interest rate risk
body: Interest rate risk arises from mismatches in rate-sensitive assets and liabilities. Types: gap (repricing) risk, basis risk (different benchmarks move differently), embedded option risk (prepayments, calls), yield curve risk (shape changes), price risk (value changes) and reinvestment risk.
Gap = rate-sensitive assets − rate-sensitive liabilities in a time bucket. A positive gap gains when rates rise; a negative gap loses. Change in net interest income ≈ gap × change in rate.
Measurement tools: maturity gap analysis, duration (and duration gap), simulation and value-at-risk.
concepts.analogy: Know whether you are asset- or liability-sensitive.
concepts.work: A bank funding long fixed loans with short deposits loses when rates rise.

concepts.title: Traditional hedges: ALM and FRAs
body: Asset-liability management (ALM) aligns maturities and repricing of assets and liabilities, setting gap limits and using internal pricing.

A forward rate agreement (FRA) fixes an interest rate for a future period on a notional amount; only the difference is settled. An A×B FRA starts in A months and ends in B months. Settlement = notional × (reference − FRA rate) × period ÷ (1 + reference × period), paid at the start.
FRA buyers (borrowers) are protected against rate rises; sellers (lenders) against falls.
concepts.analogy: An FRA locks a future borrowing or lending rate without moving principal.
concepts.work: A 3×9 FRA covers a 6-month period starting in 3 months.

concepts.title: Modern hedges: futures, options, swaps and swaptions
body: Interest rate futures are exchange-traded contracts on interest rates or bond prices; prices fall when rates rise, so borrowers hedge by selling futures.
Interest rate options: caps (protect borrowers against rates above a strike), floors (protect lenders against rates below a strike), and collars (buy a cap and sell a floor to cut premium).

Interest rate swaps exchange fixed and floating payments on a notional principal; comparative-advantage swaps create gains equal to the difference between fixed-rate and floating-rate spreads of the two parties. Swaptions are options to enter into a swap at agreed terms.
concepts.analogy: Futures and swaps lock; options insure; collars cap cost.
concepts.work: A borrower with a cap at 9% pays no more than 9% plus the premium.

illustrations.title: Gap exposure and an FRA
illustrations.q: (a) A bank has rate-sensitive assets of ₹500 crore and rate-sensitive liabilities of ₹650 crore repricing within a year. Compute the gap and the effect on net interest income of a 1% rise in rates. (b) A company buys a 3×9 FRA at 8% on ₹10 crore. At settlement, the 6-month reference rate is 9%. Compute the settlement amount (paid at the start of the period).

illustrations.title: Comparative-advantage swap
illustrations.q: Company A can borrow fixed at 8% or floating at MIBOR + 0.5%. Company B can borrow fixed at 9.5% or floating at MIBOR + 1.0%. A wants floating, B wants fixed. Compute the total gain from a swap and each party's net cost if the gain is shared equally (no intermediary).

jobs.title: Managing a bank's rate risk
jobs.situation: The bank has a large negative one-year gap and expects rate hikes.
steps: Use FRAs or swaps to reduce the gap.
jobs.takeaway: Measure the gap first, then choose the hedge.

viva.q: Why were alternative reference rates introduced?
viva.model: Because LIBOR relied on bank judgement and was manipulated; ARRs are based on actual overnight transactions.
Comparing rate-sensitive assets and liabilities in time buckets to see how rate changes affect net interest income.
It fixes a rate for a future period on a notional amount, and only the discounted interest difference is settled.
A cap protects borrowers against rates rising above a strike; a floor protects lenders against rates falling below a strike.

viva.q: Name four types of interest rate risk.
viva.model: Gap risk, basis risk, embedded option risk and yield curve risk, along with price and reinvestment risk.

cases.title: Metro Infra borrowing
cases.case: Metro Infra has a ₹200 crore floating loan at MIBOR + 1.5%, resetting annually. It enters a swap paying fixed 7% and receiving MIBOR. It also considers a cap at 8% on MIBOR costing 0.4% a year.

mcqs.explain: Pays 7 fixed + 1.5 spread; MIBOR cancels. In practice: fixed cost.
